name: Rapid Response Facility

funder.name: Rapid Response Facility (Fauna & Flora and UNESCO)

summary: Fast emergency grants to organisations responding to sudden, unforeseen threats to biodiversity at natural World Heritage sites, and occasionally other internationally recognised sites, in ODA-eligible countries.

geography.label: Countries eligible for official development assistance (OECD)

steps: Online form or downloadable form emailed to the RRF
RRF review and response (target: 8 working days)

eligibility.rule: Site is UNESCO natural or mixed World Heritage, or qualifies for an exceptional route
The project addresses a sudden emergency situation
The organisation has permission to work at the proposed site
The project lasts no more than 6 months
Can show how it respects human rights and safeguards children and vulnerable adults
The organisation can receive funds in USD into an organisational bank account from the UK
For sites outside the World Heritage network, shows the global significance of the site’s biodiversity

documents: Site authority endorsement if not the managing authority, or explain why it is unavailable
Contact details of two independent referees

status.quote: Applications are accepted throughout the year, ensuring support is available whenever emergencies arise.

applicant_types.quote: The types of organisations we fund include (but are not limited to): Government bodies responsible for site management Registered local, national or international non-governmental organisations Private sector organisations

geography.quote: RRF grants are restricted to countries that are eligible for 'official development assistance' according to the OECD.

access.quote: Requests for funding are only accepted through submission of the official RRF online application form

window.quote: Applications are accepted throughout the year, ensuring support is available whenever emergencies arise.

amount.quote: Grants of up to $40,000 to respond to emergency situations in natural World Heritage Sites.

co_finance_required.quote: Please note that match-funding is not a requirement of RRF support

effort.quote: Requests for funding are only accepted through submission of the official RRF online application form or on our downloadable form submitted to the RRF email address (rrf@fauna-flora.org).
We aim to respond to applications within 8 working days, enabling rapid deployment of resources at times of crisis.

eligibility.quote: The site is a designated UNESCO natural World Heritage site (or is designated under the mixed category). The site is on the tentative UNECSO World Heritage list (under natural or mixed category). The site directly impacts the Outstanding Universal Values (OUV) of a natural World Heritage site. The site has another international designation for its biodiversity
Applications must address a sudden emergency situation.
The RRF can make grants to any organisation that has permission to work at the proposed site.
Proposed end date* max. 6 months from start date
All organisations supported by RRF must be able to demonstrate how they ensure respect for human rights and safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults.
Applicant organisations must be able to accept funds into an organisational bank account, directly from the UK in US Dollars (USD).
Applications for actions outside the World Heritage site network must clearly demonstrate the global significance of the site’s biodiversity to be considered for funding.

documents.quote: If the applicant organisation is not the official site management authority of the proposed site you must attach an endorsement letter from the site management authority approving the project.

This is an important part of the application and is normally needed for your application to be considered. Please upload evidence of official host country endorsement of your application from the relevant site management authority* Max. file size: 256 MB. If there are specific reasons why such a letter is not available, please explain*
All applicants must include contact details of two independent referees.
